name: iFlySEO
author: jluciama

sections.description:
iFlySEO connects your WordPress blog to the iFlySEO content service. Plan your topics and keywords, generate articles with AI, review the drafts and decide when they go live.

Manage your domains at https://iflyseo.com/my-account. The web panel brings content, settings and publication status together in one place, while the plugin connects your WordPress site and handles authenticated publication to your blog.

  • Plan articles around your services, topics and keywords, with custom writing instructions.
  • Review and edit generated content before publishing, including titles, article text and SEO metadata.
  • Publish posts on demand or enable a schedule with your chosen days, time and timezone.
  • Choose WordPress authors, categories and tags where available.
  • Follow generation and publication progress, review errors and manage your word balance from the domain panel.
  • Use the plugin interface in Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian or Spanish. The article language is configured separately.

An iFlySEO account and an active service plan are required to use the content service. The plugin is free to install; content generation and other service features run on the external iFlySEO service and are subject to its plans, limits and terms. A service subscription is not included with the plugin download.

For everyday content management, use the domain panel in your iFlySEO account. You can also use the plugin administration screens in WordPress. Keep the installed plugin up to date so its WordPress connection and publication features receive updates. Switching between the web panel and WordPress does not remove existing generated content.

External services and privacy

Connecting explicitly authorizes communication with https://api.iflyseo.com to register and manage this WordPress site. Registration sends the domain, WordPress REST URL, account credentials and, when entered, the WordPress application username/password. Subsequent authenticated requests exchange publishing targets (authors and taxonomies), site settings, instructions, content, generation/publication status and diagnostics needed for the service.

Service availability and account access are enforced by the configured iFlySEO API. Calendar assets are included locally. Plugin update information is provided by WordPress.

Terms: https://iflyseo.com/en/legal/terms
Privacy: https://iflyseo.com/en/legal/privacy
Commercial terms: https://iflyseo.com/en/legal/commercial

Source and third-party libraries

The ZIP includes the unminified JavaScript and CSS alongside minified assets. WordPress supplies jQuery. Flatpickr 4.6.13 is bundled locally under the MIT license; its license is included in assets/vendor/flatpickr/LICENSE.txt.

DOMPurify 3.4.15 is bundled for HTML sanitization. Its source and licenses are included in assets/vendor/dompurify/. To rebuild the browser sanitizer from this plugin directory, install dompurify@3.4.15 and esbuild@0.28.2 with npm, then run: npx esbuild assets/js/iflyseo-html-safety.js –bundle –minify –format=iife –global-name=iflyseoHtmlSafety –target=es2020 –legal-comments=inline –outfile=assets/js/iflyseo-html-safety.min.js
sections.installation:
1. Install iFlySEO from Plugins > Add New in WordPress, or upload its ZIP with Upload Plugin, then activate it.
  2. Open iFlySEO in the WordPress administration menu and connect your iFlySEO account. If you do not have an account, register at https://iflyseo.com.
  3. Open https://iflyseo.com/my-account, select your domain and check its connection status.
  4. Choose your topics, keywords and publication settings. Generate an article, review it and publish it when you are ready, or enable a publication schedule.
sections.faq:
Do I need an iFlySEO account?

Yes. Connect an iFlySEO account with an active service plan to generate and manage content. You can review the current plans and service terms at https://iflyseo.com. Downloading the WordPress plugin does not include a service subscription.

Where can I manage my content?

Open https://iflyseo.com/my-account and select your domain. You can manage its content, instructions, word balance and publication settings there. The WordPress plugin also includes administration screens for the connected site.

Does this plugin generate articles inside WordPress?

No. Article generation runs on the external iFlySEO service. The plugin exchanges the information needed for the service and publishes authenticated content to your own WordPress site.

Can I review an article before it is published?

Yes. You can review and edit generated content before publishing it. If you enable automatic publication, articles can be published according to your selected workflow and schedule, so check those settings before enabling it.

Can I publish manually or choose publication days?

Yes. You can publish reviewed articles on demand, or enable a schedule and choose the available publication days, time and timezone from your domain settings.

Can I choose the author, categories and tags?

Yes, where those publishing targets are available on your WordPress site. The domain panel retrieves the available authors and taxonomies through the plugin connection.

Can I manage more than one WordPress site?

Yes. You can manage multiple connected domains from one iFlySEO account, within the domain limit of your service plan. Install and connect the plugin on each WordPress site you want to use.

Is iFlySEO PRO required?

No. PRO is an optional analysis service, where available, and is not required for the WordPress connection or the article-generation and publication workflow. Its availability, features and pricing depend on your account and the service terms.

Which interface languages are included?

The plugin includes interface dictionaries for Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish. WordPress.org community translations for native WordPress strings and this directory page are tracked separately from these built-in dictionaries.

Does changing the interface language change the article language?

No. The interface language and the content-generation language are configured separately.

What should I check if publication fails?

Check the domain connection and publication status in your account panel. Make sure WordPress can communicate with the iFlySEO API and that the selected author and taxonomies are still available. Review the displayed error before retrying publication.

Where can I get help?

Use the support forum at https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/iflyseo/ for plugin questions, or contact support@iflyseo.com for help with your iFlySEO account or service plan.
